description: The acceptance Mac (the owner's M1 Max): `make test` inside `nix develop`. Hosted CI runners use macos-hosted.json instead. The Mac's `make test` inside `nix develop`, classified from the 1cadaf4 record (172 skips) on 2026-09-30. naga has no rule: the dev shell provides it from stage2/nix (e74a3cc), so a naga skip is unexpected again. lldb has no rule either: the debug adapter resolves Apple's lldb without the shell's DEVELOPER_DIR and SDKROOT (stage2/lldbenv), so on a developer-mode Mac a DAP session skip is unexpected; only developer mode being off is expected. pugixml, sqlite3 and the native compiler provider have no rule since stage4/tools-ci (88a5c36) gave the Darwin dev shells pugixml, sqlite.dev and BTRC_NATIVE_PROVIDER_CC/CXX: macOS run 36934014516 ran every C++ owner, SQLite, compiler-context, receipt and consumer case, so their skips are unexpected again.

rules.reason: ^needs macOS developer mode for lldb to launch an inferior
rules.note: LldbBootstrap.debugger_access_available() found developer mode off, so lldb cannot launch an inferior without an authorization prompt. macos.yml enables it for the hosted unit shard, where the four DAP sessions run and macos-hosted.json expects no such skip; the devcontainer skips them.
Nix gcc on macOS has no libasan, and clang's ASan+UBSan runtime does not start under the dev shell; the devcontainer runs both witnesses.
windows.yml runs test_artifact_storage.py on a native Windows host.
windows.yml runs test_generation_validator_matches_native_windows_staging_modes.
windows.yml runs test_bootstrap_harness.py before its native bootstrap.
windows.yml runs test_artifact_reparse.py beside test_artifact_storage.py.
macOS resolves the cache under ~/Library/Caches; the XDG branch is Linux behavior.
macOS has no /dev/full device.
These cases link ELF objects with the Linux toolchain.

rules.reason: ^compiler wrapper does not provide its UBSan runtime$
rules.note: The macOS compiler wrapper ships no UBSan runtime.
ThreadSanitizer crashes on an independent exact-flags probe on this host.

rules.reason: ^requires Linux and the explicitly built native header reader$
rules.note: Image decoding, FreeType rasterization and audio fault injection need no display or PCM, the devcontainer's image installs a null default PCM (nix/asound.conf) for the audio sessions, and CI runs every Linux shard under tools/virtual-display.sh (Xvfb and Mesa lavapipe) for the GUI windows, GPU view and scrollbar regression. Required Linux execution is tracked separately from these Mac platform skips.

rules.reason: ^the call shapes are proven against glibc$
rules.note: glibc's transparent-union socket addresses, its variadic fcntl and the native tag aliases are proven against the Linux dev shell's sysroot through both frontends; the devcontainer's unit shard runs every case.
tools/ui/headless-session.sh starts Xvfb or weston with the AT-SPI bus from the Linux dev shell; the devcontainer's unit shard runs every case.

rules.reason: ^the (FreeType proof builds against the Linux SDK|macro proof builds against the Linux C toolchain|WebGPU proof builds against the Linux SDK)$
rules.note: The macro-constant proofs build against the Linux dev shell's C toolchain, freetype2 (pkg-config) and WebGPU headers; the devcontainer's unit shard runs both frontends (CI run 36935218617 for FreeType).

rules.reason: ^requires Linux and the explicitly built native header reader$
rules.note: The tray also needs a StatusNotifierItem watcher on a session bus, which the devcontainer lacks.
The configured-PCM capability cases run wherever ALSA headers exist.

rules.reason: ^the oracle compares against the host's own C preprocessor$
rules.note: The C oracle compares btrc's linux-x86_64 selection with the host gcc and clang -E, so only an x86_64 Linux host runs it; the devcontainer does (CL-C-06).
The real X11 and Wayland desktop check (CL-UIA-11) runs only on a physical Linux desktop, PLAN D7's host; the devcontainer skips it as awaiting hardware, so it is not covered there.

rules.reason: ^requires Windows: windows\.yml's win32-native job runs the executables the build tests publish$
rules.note: CX-UIA-15: a Linux or macOS host cross-builds the Win32 shell rows through both compilers; windows.yml's win32-native job runs them on hosted Windows x64 and ARM64.
CX-UIA-09 shell requires its host provider; both frontends and sanitizer modes run on the named stand-in.
The patched SDL's X11 clipboard path (nix/sdl3-x11-selection-requestor.patch) exists only on Linux; the probe runs under the Linux virtual display.

The Linux unit shard exercises descendants that leave the supervised session. The Android supervisor uses PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER only on Linux; macOS still runs the process-group descendant cleanup case.
The Linux btrc shard checks refusal at a 16 MiB hard stack limit and successful startup at 64 MiB. Only the launcher child changes its resource limits; macOS uses a separate compiler stack.
Real Linux ProcessThreads directory-read failure and closure, paired plain/sanitized native fixture.

rules.reason: ^requires Linux: only the Linux dev shell carries the HTTP transport's libcurl$
rules.note: libcurl (OpenSSL 3, c-ares) is the Linux HTTP transport's input (CL-P2-04); macOS uses NSURLSession, so the Darwin shells carry no libcurl. The devcontainer's unit shard builds the version probe against it.

rules.reason: ^android-(aarch64|x86_64) is NDK-bound: no toolchain for android-(aarch64|x86_64):
rules.note: The Android rows compile with the NDK's clang, which the default dev shell does not carry: nix develop .#platforms pins NDK 29.0.14206865 (Stage 23). TargetToolchain finds it through ANDROID_NDK_HOME or ANDROID_HOME/ndk/29.0.14206865 and otherwise refuses the row, never building it with the host compiler (platform-target-contract.md section 7.1: android is NDK-bound).

rules.reason: ^windows-aarch64-msvc is runner-bound: no toolchain for windows-aarch64-msvc:
rules.note: The windows-aarch64-msvc row compiles only with clang inside a Windows SDK (vcvars) environment, which only the windows-11-arm runner has (platform-target-contract.md section 1.9; runner-bound until W1).

The run mode runs the host row here and checks target_abi.expected; every other row runs in its Stage 25 host lane, on the executor its granted BTRC_TEST_CAPABILITIES capability names, which does not exist yet (platform-target-contract.md section 7.2).

Interop step 4's exit, the checked JNI round trip, runs inside app_process on an Android device. host-android.yml runs it on its API 29 and 36 x86_64 emulators with BTRC_ANDROID_JNI_REQUIRED=1, where a missing prerequisite fails; its evidence is that workflow's artifact, not a skip report. This Mac has no Android SDK; the 16 KiB-page arm64 image it could run stays MAC-P1-03.
Windows x64 and ARM64 CI execute the cross-built HTTP fixtures and retain native stdout, stderr and process status.
